questions.key_step: Shift to t=1+x; read coefficient of a binomial expansion.
questions.justification: Three routine steps (G.P. sum, re-centre, binomial coefficient); no insight beyond a familiar trick; easier than 2025-P2-Q10 (L4).

questions.key_step: Multiply b_n by a to complete (1+a)^n; telescope b_2006-b_2005.
questions.justification: Chain of closed form, subtraction and reducing 4^{2005/401}; routine multi-step, one mildly non-obvious closed form.

questions.key_step: a f(n)+(-1)^n=(a-1)^n for two parities of n.
questions.justification: Alternating closed form with sign bookkeeping for odd/even n and a fractional exponent; two linked ideas, numerical answer with no options (F2).

questions.key_step: Conjugate integer-part trick, then (I+f)F=1.
questions.justification: Standard fractional-part trick; the final f^2/(1-f) manipulation is a short extra step; routine chain.

questions.key_step: Use C(n,r)/(r+1)=C(n+1,r+1)/(n+1) and ratio of consecutive coefficients.
questions.justification: Four textbook identities, each a single familiar move; proof format adds length but not depth.

questions.key_step: Split double sum; sum C_r^2=C(200,100), sum C_r=2^100; identify m,n,p.
questions.justification: Vandermonde plus double-sum factorisation, with a precision step matching m,n,p (even); two linked ideas, no options.

questions.key_step: (sum C_i)^2 = sum C_i^2 + 2 sum_{i<j}.
questions.justification: One familiar move (square of sum), result stated in the question.

questions.key_step: S1+S2+S3 covers all ordered pairs; then minimise 2^k+200/k.
questions.justification: Two short stages: recognise the full double sum, then a divisor search; routine.

questions.key_step: P(1/x)=P(x)/x^N and P(-1)=0 because of the (1+x) factor.
questions.justification: Three parts, each needing a small idea (degree count, palindromic symmetry, x=-1 kills the sum); two ideas linked.

questions.key_step: Conjugate is negative: f=-F, so x{x}=5^89; reduce 5^89+5^178+5^267 mod 31.
questions.justification: Sign trap on the conjugate (odd power, negative), then modular order argument with exact reduction and no options; precision risk (F2) and an idea students often get wrong.

questions.key_step: Strip logs: a^{log_a b}=b; T6=21 A^2 B^5.
questions.justification: Log simplification then one equation in 3^{|x-2|}; routine chain.

questions.key_step: Evaluate sum as 4^10+10*2^9; then f(1)<0, f(5)<0.
questions.justification: Two unrelated standard ideas linked (binomial sums, root location), each routine; numerical answer.

questions.key_step: Roots-of-unity filter for every third coefficient.
questions.justification: Standard Advanced technique but not routine for all students (idea availability); short once known.

questions.key_step: n from sum of coefficients; R(1-f)=R*F conjugate.
questions.justification: Two stages (find n, conjugate trick) with an exact value; option check available.

questions.key_step: Greatest-term formula, or note terms equal C(8,r) at x=1/2.
questions.justification: Single familiar formula applied after n is known from the paragraph.

questions.key_step: Coefficients are C(8,r)2^r, so max is a tie at r=5,6, not the middle.
questions.justification: Trap: the 'middle term' belief gives the wrong set; requires checking the tie.

questions.key_step: x=1 and x=-1 separate even and odd coefficients.
questions.justification: One familiar trick applied once.

questions.key_step: x=i: real part of (3+4i)^n with polar form.
questions.justification: Complex numbers inside a binomial coefficient question; idea (x=i) is less common than x=-1; options help.
Follows directly from the previous part once x=i is seen; routine.
